newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan seeks better bids in Nat Grid tender.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan seeks better bids in Nat Grid tender.

text.p: A tender for a 25-year contract to manage Kazakhstan's national power grid has been delayed because the government wants the two bidders to improve their offers, a privatisation official said on Monday.
Britain's National Grid Group and Sweden's ABB AB, who are competing for the tender, had expected the result to be announced late on Friday.
"Each side has been asked to improve their offers," Galymzhan Nurkasimov, a senior official at the state privatisation committee, told Reuters.

Galymzhanov said conditions of the deal were confidential but noted that the former Soviet republic's national grid totalled 16,000 km (10,000 miles) and the management contract would be granted for 25 years.
The Kazakh government is anxious to speed up privatisation to raise cash to boost hard-hit state coffers, but tender results like these are often subject to delay and last minute haggling.
The government has said the national grid was strategically important and would not be privatised.
